title: FastAPI : créer une API REST en Python
desc: Construis une API moderne avec validation automatique, documentation Swagger et async natif.
content:
## Introduction

FastAPI est le framework Python le plus rapide pour construire des APIs. Validation automatique, docs générées, async natif.

## Installation

```bash
pip install fastapi uvicorn[standard] pydantic
```

## API de base

```python
from fastapi import FastAPI, HTTPException
from pydantic import BaseModel
from typing import Optional

app = FastAPI(title="Mon API", version="1.0.0")

class User(BaseModel):
    name: str
    email: str
    age: Optional[int] = None

class UserResponse(User):
    id: int

users_db = {}

@app.get("/users", response_model=list[UserResponse])
async def get_users():
    return list(users_db.values())

@app.post("/users", response_model=UserResponse, status_code=201)
async def create_user(user: User):
    user_id = len(users_db) + 1
    new_user = UserResponse(id=user_id, **user.model_dump())
    users_db[user_id] = new_user
    return new_user

@app.get("/users/{user_id}")
async def get_user(user_id: int):
    if user_id not in users_db:
        raise HTTPException(status_code=404, detail="Utilisateur non trouvé")
    return users_db[user_id]
```

## Démarrer

```bash
uvicorn main:app --reload
# Docs : http://localhost:8000/docs
# Redoc : http://localhost:8000/redoc
```

## Dépendances et authentification

```python
from fastapi import Depends
from fastapi.security import HTTPBearer, HTTPAuthorizationCredentials

security = HTTPBearer()

def verify_token(credentials: HTTPAuthorizationCredentials = Depends(security)):
    token = credentials.credentials
    if token != "mon-secret":
        raise HTTPException(status_code=401, detail="Token invalide")
    return token

@app.get("/protected")
async def protected_route(token: str = Depends(verify_token)):
    return {"message": "Accès autorisé"}
```

## Conclusion

FastAPI génère automatiquement la doc OpenAPI. Ajoute SQLAlchemy ou Tortoise ORM pour la persistance.

title: Docker : conteneuriser une application Node.js
desc: Empaquète ton app Node.js dans un conteneur Docker optimisé pour la production.
content:
## Introduction

Docker garantit que ton app tourne de la même façon partout : en dev, en test et en prod.

## Dockerfile optimisé

```dockerfile
# Build stage
FROM node:20-alpine AS builder
WORKDIR /app

# Copier les manifestes en premier (cache Docker)
COPY package*.json ./
RUN npm ci --only=production

# Copier le code
COPY . .
RUN npm run build

# Production stage
FROM node:20-alpine AS production
WORKDIR /app

# Utilisateur non-root pour la sécurité
RUN addgroup -S appgroup && adduser -S appuser -G appgroup

COPY --from=builder /app/dist ./dist
COPY --from=builder /app/node_modules ./node_modules
COPY --from=builder /app/package.json .

USER appuser
EXPOSE 3000

CMD ["node", "dist/index.js"]
```

## .dockerignore

```
node_modules
.git
.env
*.log
dist
.DS_Store
```

## docker-compose.yml

```yaml
version: '3.9'

services:
  app:
    build: .
    ports:
      - "3000:3000"
    environment:
      - NODE_ENV=production
      - DATABASE_URL=postgresql://postgres:secret@db:5432/mydb
    depends_on:
      db:
        condition: service_healthy

  db:
    image: postgres:17-alpine
    environment:
      POSTGRES_DB: mydb
      POSTGRES_PASSWORD: secret
    volumes:
      - postgres_data:/var/lib/postgresql/data
    healthcheck:
      test: ["CMD-SHELL", "pg_isready -U postgres"]
      interval: 5s
      timeout: 5s
      retries: 5

volumes:
  postgres_data:
```

## Commandes utiles

```bash
# Build
docker build -t mon-app .

# Run
docker run -p 3000:3000 --env-file .env mon-app

# Compose
docker compose up -d
docker compose logs -f app
docker compose down

# Debug
docker exec -it <container_id> sh
docker stats
```

## Conclusion

Multi-stage builds réduisent l'image de 1GB à ~150MB. Utilise Docker Compose pour le dev local et Kubernetes pour orchestrer en prod.

title: PostgreSQL : requêtes avancées et optimisations
desc: Maîtrise les CTEs, les window functions, les index et EXPLAIN pour des requêtes SQL performantes.
content:
## Introduction

PostgreSQL est bien plus qu'une base de données basique. Ces fonctionnalités avancées éliminent des dizaines de requêtes et calculs côté applicatif.

## CTEs (Common Table Expressions)

```sql
-- Calculer les top 5 clients par CA
WITH customer_revenue AS (
  SELECT
    c.id,
    c.name,
    SUM(o.amount) AS total_revenue,
    COUNT(o.id)   AS order_count
  FROM customers c
  JOIN orders o ON o.customer_id = c.id
  WHERE o.created_at >= NOW() - INTERVAL '1 year'
  GROUP BY c.id, c.name
),
ranked AS (
  SELECT *, RANK() OVER (ORDER BY total_revenue DESC) AS rank
  FROM customer_revenue
)
SELECT * FROM ranked WHERE rank <= 5;
```

## Window Functions

```sql
-- Calculer la progression mensuelle
SELECT
  month,
  revenue,
  LAG(revenue) OVER (ORDER BY month) AS prev_month,
  revenue - LAG(revenue) OVER (ORDER BY month) AS growth,
  AVG(revenue) OVER (ORDER BY month ROWS BETWEEN 2 PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW) AS moving_avg_3m
FROM monthly_revenue
ORDER BY month;

-- Numéroter les lignes par groupe
SELECT
  category,
  product,
  sales,
  ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY category ORDER BY sales DESC) AS rank_in_category
FROM products;
```

## Index et optimisations

```sql
-- Index simple
CREATE INDEX idx_users_email ON users(email);

-- Index composite (ordre important !)
CREATE INDEX idx_orders_user_date ON orders(user_id, created_at DESC);

-- Index partiel (seulement les publiés)
CREATE INDEX idx_tutorials_published ON tutorials(created_at DESC)
WHERE published = true;

-- Index full-text search
CREATE INDEX idx_tutorials_fts ON tutorials
USING gin(to_tsvector('french', title || ' ' || description));

-- Recherche FTS
SELECT * FROM tutorials
WHERE to_tsvector('french', title || ' ' || description)
    @@ plainto_tsquery('french', 'machine learning');
```

## EXPLAIN ANALYZE

```sql
EXPLAIN (ANALYZE, BUFFERS, FORMAT JSON)
SELECT * FROM orders
WHERE user_id = 123
ORDER BY created_at DESC
LIMIT 10;

-- Chercher :
-- Seq Scan → potentiellement lent, ajouter un index
-- Index Scan → bien
-- Nested Loop → ok pour petits sets
-- Hash Join → ok pour grands sets
```

## Conclusion

Un index bien placé peut multiplier les performances par 100x. Utilise `pg_stat_user_indexes` pour repérer les index inutilisés.

title: CI/CD avec GitHub Actions
desc: Automatise tes tests, builds et déploiements avec GitHub Actions sur chaque push.
content:
## Introduction

GitHub Actions automatise tout le cycle de vie : tests, linting, build et déploiement. Gratuit pour les repos publics.

## Pipeline de base

```yaml
# .github/workflows/ci.yml
name: CI

on:
  push:
    branches: [main, develop]
  pull_request:
    branches: [main]

jobs:
  test:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    
    services:
      postgres:
        image: postgres:17
        env:
          POSTGRES_PASSWORD: test
          POSTGRES_DB: testdb
        options: >-
          --health-cmd pg_isready
          --health-interval 10s
          --health-timeout 5s
          --health-retries 5
    
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      
      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: '20'
          cache: 'npm'
      
      - run: npm ci
      - run: npm run lint
      - run: npm run type-check
      - run: npm test
        env:
          DATABASE_URL: postgresql://postgres:test@localhost:5432/testdb
```

## Build et push Docker

```yaml
  build:
    needs: test
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    if: github.ref == 'refs/heads/main'
    
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      
      - uses: docker/login-action@v3
        with:
          registry: ghcr.io
          username: ${{ github.actor }}
          password: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
      
      - uses: docker/build-push-action@v5
        with:
          push: true
          tags: ghcr.io/${{ github.repository }}:latest
          cache-from: type=gha
          cache-to: type=gha,mode=max
```

## Déploiement Railway

```yaml
  deploy:
    needs: build
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      
      - name: Deploy to Railway
        run: |
          npm install -g @railway/cli
          railway deploy --service YourTuto
        env:
          RAILWAY_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.RAILWAY_TOKEN }}
```

## Secrets et environnements

```yaml
# Utiliser des secrets dans les steps
env:
  API_KEY: ${{ secrets.API_KEY }}
  DATABASE_URL: ${{ secrets.DATABASE_URL }}

# Environnements avec protection
environment:
  name: production
  url: https://monapp.com
```

## Conclusion

Un bon pipeline CI/CD évite les déploiements cassés. Commence simple : lint + tests + deploy. Ajoute complexity ensuite.
